daily_brief: The most consequential development today is Saudi Arabia's shutdown of its critical East-West oil pipeline following drone attacks launched from Iraq [BBC], [France 24], [The Hindu], a move that removes 4-5% of global oil supply from a key bypass route around the Strait of Hormuz amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict now in its seventh month. This compounds existing pressure on global energy markets as Iranian-backed Houthi rebels consolidate territorial gains near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Meanwhile, BRICS leaders convened in New Delhi [France 24], [RFI], [Nikkei Asia], [Al Jazeera] with host India working to bridge divisions between Iran and the UAE to secure a joint statement, as the bloc seeks greater influence amid Western tensions. President Trump's two-day Ireland visit [BBC], [France 24] drew thousands of protesters and highlighted ongoing friction over his blending of official duties with personal business interests at his Doonbeg golf resort. The US marked the 25th anniversary of 9/11 with ceremonies featuring all living presidents [BBC], [RFI], while Trump used the occasion to link the original attacks to his current Iran campaign. French investigators suspect sabotage in a Normandy train derailment that injured 44 people [France 24], adding to European security concerns.

top_stories.headline: Saudi Arabia Shuts Critical Oil Pipeline After Drone Attacks From Iraq
bullets: Saudi Arabia closed its 1,200km East-West pipeline after drone attacks originating from Iraqi territory, with Baghdad acknowledging the strikes came from a province bordering Iran and firing a military commander in response
The pipeline, built in the 1980s, carries 4-5% of global oil supply and serves as a crucial bypass route around the Strait of Hormuz during the ongoing US-Iran conflict now in its seventh month
Saudi Arabia chose not to retaliate following a call from Iraq's prime minister but reserved the right to take future measures to protect its sovereignty and facilities

The shutdown compounds pressure on global energy markets as Iranian-backed Houthi rebels have made their biggest territorial gains in years near Yemen's coast, threatening the Bab el-Mandeb shipping strait

top_stories.headline: BRICS Leaders Convene in New Delhi Amid Wars and US Tensions
bullets: Leaders of the 11-nation BRICS bloc gathered in India for a two-day summit focused on trade, investment, and expanding the group's influence in global affairs
Indian Prime Minister Modi hosted Russian President Putin, Chinese President Xi, and Iranian President Pezeshkian amid heightened security with thousands of police deployed across New Delhi

The summit faces challenges in achieving unity as wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, plus US-China tensions, create competing priorities among members with sharply different foreign policy interests
Officials expressed optimism about issuing a joint declaration, with host India working to bridge differences between Iran and the UAE over the Persian Gulf crisis

top_stories.headline: Trump Visits Ireland for Diplomacy and Golf Tournament at His Resort
bullets: President Trump arrived in Dublin for a two-day visit including meetings with Irish President Catherine Connolly and Taoiseach Micheál Martin, triggering one of the largest security operations in Irish history with 4,000 personnel deployed

Irish President Connolly, an outspoken Gaza activist who previously called Trump a 'bully' over tariffs, faced pressure from Irish political parties to raise Middle East issues during her meeting with the US president
Trump will attend the Amgen Irish Open golf tournament at his Trump International Golf Links and Hotel Doonbeg, which he owns, and may present the trophy on Sunday
Thousands of anti-Trump protesters planned rallies in Dublin as critics highlighted the visit as another example of the president blending official duties with personal business interests

top_stories.headline: US Marks 25th Anniversary of September 11 Attacks
bullets: President Trump led a Pentagon ceremony while Vice President Vance joined all four living former presidents—Bush, Obama, Biden, and Clinton—at the World Trade Center memorial in New York

Moments of silence marked the timing of each attack and the names of nearly 3,000 victims were read aloud; organizers added a seventh moment of silence for the first time to honor over 9,400 people who have died from illnesses linked to toxic exposure at Ground Zero
The CIA declassified intelligence briefs about Al-Qaeda coinciding with the anniversary
Trump used the occasion to link the original 'war on terror' to his current conflict with Iran, stating the Islamic Republic 'will never, ever have a nuclear weapon'

top_stories.headline: French Investigators Suspect Sabotage in Normandy Train Derailment
bullets: A train carrying 186 passengers derailed between Rouen and Caen in northwest France on Friday evening, injuring 44 people including an 18-year-old woman in critical condition
Investigators found a fragment of rail on the track and are treating sabotage as the main line of inquiry
Authorities activated a mass-casualty response with 130 firefighters, five medical teams, and 80 vehicles; the train driver tested negative for drugs and alcohol
Traffic on the line has been suspended and power to the tracks cut as the investigation continues
